tokens.text: // A kernel quote is the one place Musa lets a composer write the assembly the
// compiler normally writes for them. `kernel EventTrack[WrittenTime, ScoreFact] { ... }` is a
// composition expression of the temporal kernel — the same grammar a
// `.musa.kernel` file is written in — and `${...}` splices ordinary Musa music
// into it. What it buys is placement no surface constructor spells; what it
// costs is stated at the bottom of this file.
// Ordinary music, checked the ordinary way. Nothing about it knows it is
// One term, assembled by hand. `${subject}` is a hole: it is instantiated
// once, here, under this piece's context, and bound to a fresh name the
// compiler chooses — so nothing written inside the quote can capture it,
// whatever the quote happens to call its own bindings.
// `subj` is referenced three times and elaborated once. That is sharing, and
// it is why the three references below are three placements of the *same*
// facts rather than three re-readings of `subject`.
// Diminution, a measure later. The halving is written in the
// host, not as a raw `scale by`: renotating is a payload
// operation and the kernel never touches payloads, so raw scaling
// would move these notes without changing what is written on
// them. A second hole is a second instantiation, and gets a locus
// Observation: the fourth note alone, read out of the material
// through a window and placed at the start of the last measure.
// Restricting keeps the extent, so this branch still runs to 2.
// Raw material, written as facts. A payload states what the
// material *is*; it states no scope and no origin, because the
// use decides which voice this lands in and the quote is where it
// came from. Writing either is refused.
// The guarantees the quote keeps are exact time and payload
// typing: the term's extent is 2 whole notes, computed from
// its structure, and every payload in it is a `ScoreFact`.
// The guarantees it does *not* keep are the theory ones, and
// an assertion around the completed quote is how they come
// back. This claim is checked against the assembled facts, so
// it sees the raw notes and the spliced ones alike.
// What a quote gives up, precisely:
// A hole is instantiated once and the facts it produced are frozen from
// then on. A raw `shift`, `scale` or `restrict` around a reference moves
// facts that already exist; it does not re-elaborate the hole under the
// context the reference sits in. So an assertion that passed *inside*
// `subject` — that it fills a measure, say — says nothing about the
// diminished copy above, which fills half of one. Bar alignment, scale
// membership and chord realization are properties of where facts land,
// and raw placement is exactly the freedom to land them elsewhere.
// and `restrict` want nothing of the payloads and are safe to write here;
// `scale` halves every span and leaves every written value alone, which
// is why the diminution above is spelled `${stretch(1/2, subject)}` and
// not `scale by 1/2`. Raw scaling is for material whose written values
// Every fact that leaves a quote records a `splice` step in its expansion
// path, at the locus it was assembled at, so Origin can say that a note
// with no surface statement behind it came from here.
